# Cūḷasuvajātaka (Ja 430)

**ID:** Ja 430
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Cūḷasuvajātaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul8.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cūḷasuvajātaka* (Ja 430), also known as the *Cullasukajātakam* and translated as "The Shorter Tale of King Parrot," is a Buddhist birth-story preserved in the Pali Jātaka collection [Anandajoti 2010]. According to its opening frame story at Jetavana in Sāvatthī, the Buddha related this past-life narrative after the monks praised his extraordinary contentment and lack of covetousness during a difficult rains retreat at Verañja, where he had subsisted merely on water and ground roots because Māra prevented him from receiving alms. In the story of the past, Sakka tests the contentment and loyalty of a parrot by withering the tree it dwells in; although all other birds abandon the dead tree, the parrot remains faithful to its longtime refuge, prompting Sakka—disguised as a goose—to engage the bird in a verse dialogue celebrating faithfulness in friendship [Anandajoti 2010].

In his study of the Dhammapada commentary, Eugene W. Burlingame notes that the commentary cites this story when discussing frugality, quoting the opening verse of Ja 430 and directing the reader to the tenth *nipāta*; while V. Fausböll places the story in the ninth *nipāta*, its ten stanzas confirm that it stood in the tenth *nipāta* in the Jātaka recension known to the Dhammapada commentator [Burlingame 1921]. The narrative and its verses are intimately paired with the immediately preceding *Mahāsuvajātaka* (Ja 429), which shares the same underlying story and with which it shares several lines of text reuse (§9.1–11.1 corresponding to Ja 429 §8.4–11.1) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records extensive Pali-internal text reuse with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, as well as machine-detected alignments with the Tibetan translation of the *Rāṣṭrapālaparipṛcchā-sūtra* (D0062) [DharmaNexus].

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Tatiyo bhāgo) (Atk S0513a3) (§1.1–10.4 ↔ §4432_8–4462); Mahāsuvajātaka (Ja 429) (§9.1–11.1 ↔ §8.4–11.1)
- Cross-language matches (DharmaNexus): BO_K08_D0062_H0062 [bo]; འཕགས་པ་གང་པོས་ཞུས་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོའི་མདོ (ārya-rāṣtrapālaparipṛcchā-nāma-mahāyānasūtra) (D0062) [bo]
